patterns.pattern: Access to data is restricted based on user role or relationship to the data (e.g., only admins, owners, specified users, or related parties may view, modify, or manage certain resources).
patterns.example_phrasing: Only users with appropriate roles or permissions can view or modify sensitive data or resources.

patterns.pattern: Sensitive user or system data must be encrypted and securely stored to ensure confidentiality and integrity.
patterns.example_phrasing: All user data is encrypted and securely stored to prevent unauthorized access.

patterns.pattern: User authentication is required before granting access to the system or sensitive actions, typically via unique credentials (username/password or similar).
patterns.example_phrasing: User must authenticate with a unique username and password before accessing the system.

patterns.pattern: A resource (e.g., username, identifier) must be unique within its context; duplicates are disallowed.
patterns.example_phrasing: No two users may have the same username; identifiers must be unique.

patterns.pattern: Monetary/account balances and numeric fields must always remain within specified non-negative or valid ranges.
patterns.example_phrasing: User balance must not fall below zero and amounts must be positive.

patterns.pattern: State transitions follow strict business lifecycles (e.g., 'delivered' only after certain steps; statuses reflect order in process).
patterns.example_phrasing: A package can only move to 'delivered' status after being signed by the recipient.

patterns.pattern: System errors or invalid operations return clear error messages and do not proceed (e.g., invalid input, unavailable resources).
patterns.example_phrasing: If an incorrect command or invalid data is given, show an error message.

patterns.pattern: Access to files, data, or actions can be restricted or granted based on combinations of user, role, IP address, time/date, group, or other policy rules.
patterns.example_phrasing: Files may be restricted to certain users or groups, or automatically unlocked after a set date.

patterns.pattern: Minimum or required metadata/information is enforced for submitted entities (datasets, licenses, reservations, etc.).
patterns.example_phrasing: A minimum set of metadata is required when submitting a new dataset.

patterns.pattern: Operational or regulated compliance standards must be met (e.g., industry regulations, accessibility, uptime, data protection laws).
patterns.example_phrasing: The product must comply with required industry and accessibility regulations.

patterns.pattern: Uniqueness or limits for active instances or sessions (e.g., only one user per machine, one product instance at a time).
patterns.example_phrasing: Only one instance of the product may run per system at a time.

patterns.pattern: Actions or results must complete within defined performance constraints (e.g., queries must finish within n seconds, application responses under m seconds).
patterns.example_phrasing: Searches must return results within a specified number of seconds.

patterns.pattern: Original or source data cannot be modified or deleted without special permission or audit trail.
patterns.example_phrasing: Original data is protected from modification or deletion.

patterns.pattern: Deleted or modified resources are either restorable or must be tracked for provenance or auditability.
patterns.example_phrasing: Deleted files can be recovered, and all changes are tracked for auditing.

patterns.pattern: Data and processes must conform to defined schemas, formats, or standards, with normalization as required for consistency.
patterns.example_phrasing: All data must be validated against the declared schema and normalized for consistency.

patterns.pattern: Certain roles or users are the only ones permitted to perform administrative or sensitive actions (e.g., block users, update ratings, onboard information, etc.).
patterns.example_phrasing: Only administrators or specified privileged users may update sensitive system settings.

patterns.pattern: Security features must include protections against common threats (e.g., virus, denial of service, credential recovery restrictions, clipboard clearing).
patterns.example_phrasing: Passwords copied to clipboard are cleared after a short interval for security.

patterns.pattern: System functions must run in common environments and with only permitted dependencies; external or non-specified libraries are disallowed.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only specified standard libraries are allowed; custom dependencies are not permitted.

patterns.pattern: Lifecycle actions are atomic when required (e.g., reconfiguration or upgrades must happen all-or-nothing).
patterns.example_phrasing: Reconfiguration applies to all settings at once or not at all.

patterns.pattern: Data and processes may be placed under temporary restriction or embargo and become public or accessible after certain conditions/times.
patterns.example_phrasing: Datasets can be embargoed until a specified date before being made public.
